 When do clocks ‘fall back’ in the US? Daylight saving time ends soon
 Brittney Donovan Monday 19 October 2026 09:43 BST 
 Bookmark popover
 Removed from bookmarks
 Close popover The U.S. has repeatedly moved to end the clock change but has so far been unsuccessful ( Getty Images ) Most of the United States will “fall back” on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 2 a.m. (ET) as daylight saving time ends, meaning Americans will get an extra hour of sleep after Halloween.
 The clock change is a hotly contested issue in the states, though legislative efforts to halt it for good have failed for years.
 A study from Stanford University revealed that switching clocks back and forth twice a year is the worst option for human health, supporting long-standing calls from major medical groups to adopt permanent standard time. 
 Researchers say standard time aligns more naturally with human biology and circadian rhythms by providing essential morning sunlight, which resets the internal clock and synchronizes key organ systems. 
 Even a single hour shift can disrupt sleep schedules and worsen chronic sleep deprivation, with spring changes specifically linked to immediate spikes in car crashes, heart attacks, and mood disruptions.
